title: Moroccan Chicken Chickpea Tray
seoTitle: Moroccan Chicken Chickpea Tray | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Warm-spiced thighs with chickpeas, apricots, and roasted carrots
subtitle: Warm-spiced thighs with chickpeas, apricots, and roasted carrots
description: Chicken thighs roast with chickpeas, carrots, dried apricots, and ras el hanout-inspired spices until fragrant and caramelized.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Moroccan Chicken Chickpea Tray in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix spice blend
steps.instruction: Combine cumin, cinnamon, ginger, paprika, garlic, salt, and olive oil into a paste that coats a spoon without separating. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Coat chicken and vegetables
steps.instruction: Toss thighs, chickpeas, carrots, onion, and apricots with spice paste until every piece looks evenly coated and lightly glossy. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Roast until chicken is done
steps.instruction: Spread on two half-sheets in a single layer. Roast at 425°F 32–38 minutes until chicken reads 165°F and chickpeas crisp at edges. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and check texture
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes. Apricots should be plump and lightly caramelized; carrots tender with slight bite at the center. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Serve with couscous
steps.instruction: Portion chicken with chickpea mixture. Pan should smell warm-spiced, not burnt; chicken juices should run clear. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Ras el hanout blend works if you have it—use 2 tbsp instead of individual spices.
Offer harissa at the line for heat without changing the base tray.
Couscous cooks in 5 minutes—ideal side while tray rests.
tonightSpread: Plain Greek yogurt for cooling contrast.
leftovers: Moroccan grain bowl with leftover couscous and chickpeas.
Shred chicken into a wrap with hummus spread.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Adventurous flavor without exotic equipment. Sweet apricots balance warm spices for broad crew appeal.
mealPrepNotes: Mix spice blend in bulk for future trays. Soak apricots 10 minutes if very dry. Station: Drain and pat chickpeas dry—they crisp better when not dripping. Station: Use two pans so chickpeas roast instead of steam under crowded chicken. Station: Scatter fresh cilantro at the line, not before hold—herbs wilt in hot pans.
